newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Serbs stop counting votes from Bosnia poll.
newsitem.headline: Serbs stop counting votes from Bosnia poll.

text.p: Bosnian Serb authorities have instructed their officials to stop counting votes from Saturday's countrywide elections, a spokeswoman for international poll organisers said on Sunday.

"The president of the Republika Srpska (RS) election commission has sent a letter to counting stations in the RS asking them to stop counting," Nicole Szulc, spokeswoman for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe said.
Szulc said she had no other details, but that an OSCE team led by its director of elections Jeff Fischer had left for the Serb-stronghold of Pale to try and resolve the issue.
Slobodan Kovac, chairman of the RS electoral commission, is not a member of the Provisional Election Commission overseeing the poll, but has the authority to order a halt to counting in his area.
The Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) said on Saturday it would not accept the results in the Serb Republic due to voting irregularities.
Analysts said the Serb move was probably a counter-move heralding the start of an intensive bout of post-election manoeuvring.
